label: Nav Arrow
title: Nav Arrow
summary: Use a Nav Arrow to show that something leads elsewhere: a chevron at the end of a row, or a back arrow in a header.
corePrinciple: A cue, not a button. Make the whole row pressable, and give the arrow onPress only when it stands alone.

anatomy.title: A chevron with an optional target
anatomy.description: The arrow is a 2 px stroked chevron. Give it onPress and it gains a 44 × 44 pressable area; without it, it is a small image.
blocks: A 6 × 10 px chevron with a 2 px rounded grey stroke.
With onPress, a 44 × 44 area surrounds the chevron.

anatomy.note: A 6 × 10 px chevron with a 2 px rounded grey stroke.
With onPress, a 44 × 44 area surrounds the chevron.

configuration.title: Point where it leads
configuration.description: Forward leads to another screen, Back returns to the previous one, and Down opens content below.
blocks: At the end of a row. ListItem draws it for you.
Beside a screen title, as its own button.
Next to a label that opens more content below.

examples.title: Forward

examples.title: Back
examples.description: Beside a screen title, as its own button.

examples.title: Down

states.title: Decorative or pressable
states.description: Without onPress the arrow is an image inside something pressable. With onPress it is a button that dims to 70% while pressed. It has no disabled look.
blocks: A 6 × 10 image; the row around it handles presses.
A 44 × 44 button; press it to see it dim.

examples.title: Decorative
examples.description: A 6 × 10 image; the row around it handles presses.

examples.title: Pressable
examples.description: A 44 × 44 button; press it to see it dim.

sizing.title: Small chevron, 44 px target
sizing.description: The chevron is 6 × 10 px (10 × 6 pointing down). A pressable arrow reserves 44 × 44 px so it is easy to tap.

content.title: Name the destination
content.description: The arrow has no visible text. When it is a button, set accessibilityLabel to where it goes, such as “Back to Home”, instead of the default “Go back”.

inContext.title: A header and a list of accounts
inContext.description: The back arrow is its own button; each row is pressable as a whole and ListItem draws its forward arrow. The screen handles the navigation.

doDont.title: A clear cue in the right place
doDont.description: Each pair shows an arrow that guides people versus one that misleads them.
blocks: The label and the arrow both open Statements.

sources.title: Use the public Nav Arrow contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.77 from the team’s private package repository. List Item, App Bar, Section, and Summary Tile already draw their own arrows. A decorative arrow is still announced as an image, and a disabled arrow looks the same as an enabled one. In Dark colour mode the chevron currently turns orange because of a token value, so use it on light surfaces.
